The Blazor Web App is ready at `/tmp/sv-52e361297368408392a29904cf0a6ee6/ShipmentTracker/`. Here's what was built:

**Architecture:** Blazor Auto render mode — pages SSR on first visit (fast load), then switch to WebAssembly (no server round-trips for interactivity).

**Key pages (all `InteractiveAuto`):**
| Page | Route | Access |
|---|---|---|
| Home | `/` | Public, shows role-aware cards |
| Track Shipment | `/track` | Public — enter tracking # to see status + ETA |
| My Shipments | `/my-shipments` | Authenticated — shows shipments for logged-in user |
| Dispatcher Dashboard | `/dispatcher` | `Dispatcher` role — full CRUD, filter, search |

**Auth:** ASP.NET Core Identity with roles (`Dispatcher`, `Customer`). Seeded demo accounts:
- `dispatcher@shiptrack.io` / `Dispatch1!`
- `customer@example.com` / `Customer1!`

**Data:** EF Core + SQLite with 5 sample shipments, Minimal API endpoints under `/api/`.

Run with `cd ShipmentTracker/ShipmentTracker && dotnet run`.
